_README: Declared windows during which OPENROUTER_LIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED may be on,
and during which the LLM judge may be on alongside it.
This file is the machine-readable form of ADR-0060's revert condition, which
was prose and which nothing executed. It is read by two checks:
1. scripts/live_posture_check.py, run every 30 minutes by
.github/workflows/live-posture-watchdog.yml against what PRODUCTION
actually serves. If production reports a live posture that no window
below covers and attends, the watchdog opens an issue and the job goes
red.
2. tests/unit/test_live_execution_posture_declaration.py, which runs in
the blocking `pytest (Python 3.12)` lane and refuses a fly.toml that
sets the flag to "true" with no window covering the merge.
TO OPEN A WINDOW: add an entry to `windows` in the SAME pull request that
sets the flag. Every entry needs owner, reason, mode, judge and opened_at.
FIELDS
owner     who is attending this window. A real person.
reason    why. A real reason.
mode      "time_boxed" or "standing". Nothing else parses — an
unrecognised mode makes the whole file untrusted rather than
being ignored, so a typo cannot silently disable the field.
judge     REQUIRED boolean, and a real boolean: is the LLM judge part of
this window? There is no default, because a defaulted money
field is a decision nobody made. The judge is a SECOND paid
subsystem and its GET-path spend reaches no ledger (ADR-0013),
so global_daily_spend_usd under-reports by exactly its cost
while it runs. If /status reports judge_enabled=true during a
live posture and no attended window says "judge": true, the
watchdog alerts.
opened_at when the window starts. ISO-8601 with an explicit offset.
expires_at REQUIRED for time_boxed, FORBIDDEN for standing.
adr       REQUIRED for standing, FORBIDDEN for time_boxed. See below.
reaffirm_issue  optional issue number where re-affirmations are posted.
Without it a window cannot be re-affirmed and lapses after the
cadence — which is fine, and deliberate, for a window shorter
than a day.
RE-AFFIRMATION — this replaces a maximum window length
A window is sanctioned only while somebody is still attending it. The clock
starts at opened_at and is reset by a human re-affirmation. Past
REAFFIRMATION_CADENCE_HOURS (24h) with no reset, the window stops
sanctioning anything and the watchdog alerts, at ANY length. That is why
there is deliberately still NO maximum window length here: the #357 failure
ran ~3 days and issue #105 legitimately needs ~7 days of production logs, so
no single number separates them. "Is anybody still watching?" does.
TO RE-AFFIRM, comment on the window's reaffirm_issue:
REAFFIRM live-execution 2026-08-25T09:00:00+00:00
quoting the window's own opened_at, so one comment attends one window. The
comment must come from the account named as that window's `owner`. Ordinary
Markdown in front of it is fine — a backtick, a '> ' quote, a bullet — but
the token has to START the line, so quoting it inside a sentence does not
count.
A window whose cover can outlive the cadence MUST name a reaffirm_issue;
one shorter than the cadence needs nothing.
It is a COMMENT and not a field in this file on purpose. GitHub sets both
the author type and the timestamp, and the commenter sets neither: a comment
posted by any workflow token — INCLUDING THIS WATCHDOG'S OWN — is typed
"Bot" by GitHub and is refused, as is anything posted through a GitHub
App, and a re-affirmation cannot be forward-dated to never lapse. A
committed field would have had neither property here: no commit in this
repository is signed, most commits already carry a bot-shaped committer via
the squash-merge path, and a workflow with contents: write already exists
and has pushed.
WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, stated because the first draft of this file
overstated it: that a HUMAN acted. user.type is the type of the ACCOUNT, so
a personal access token posts as "User" and would pass. What it does
prove is that no DEFAULT automation re-affirmed. Note also that opened_at is
a field in THIS file, so moving it forward resets the attention clock with
no comment at all — bounded, reported every cycle, and not closed. ADR-0071
records both residuals.
MODE: standing
"standing" has no expiry and exists for the steady state, once live
execution is permanent rather than an event. It REMOVES THE DEADLINE AND
NOTHING ELSE — a standing window still needs re-affirming every 24h, so
setting `standing` to quiet a noisy alert buys a day, never silence. It must
cite an ADR, and the citation is resolved rather than trusted: the ADR must
exist in docs/adr/, be Accepted, carry the line
**Authorises:** OPENROUTER_LIVE_EXECUTION_ENABLED
on its own, and NOT be ADR-0070 or ADR-0071 — a mechanism may not authorise
its own use, so going permanently live costs the ADR that says so. A standing
window is also never silent: the watchdog reports it by name every cycle,
because a standing posture that produced silence would be indistinguishable
from a dead watchdog.
TIMESTAMPS are ISO-8601 and MUST carry an explicit offset; a naive one is
refused rather than assigned a zone. Any offset is accepted and normalised
to UTC for display, so prefer a plain Z: `2026-08-26T00:00:00-12:00` ends
twelve hours later than it looks. A window is active when
opened_at <= now < expires_at. A malformed entry makes the whole file
unreadable and both checks alert — a declaration that cannot be parsed must
never be mistaken for a declaration that permits something.
Leave expired entries in place: they are the record of what was sanctioned.
WORKED EXAMPLES (not active — this file's `windows` list is empty):
time_boxed:
{"owner": "you", "reason": "why", "mode": "time_boxed",
"judge": false, "opened_at": "2026-08-25T09:00:00Z",
"expires_at": "2026-08-25T17:00:00Z", "reaffirm_issue": 105}
standing:
{"owner": "you", "reason": "GA", "mode": "standing",
"adr": "ADR-0080", "reaffirm_issue": 400}

windows.reason: Measure W1 streaming live: does usage arrive without stream_options, is [DONE] sent, do all four default models honour stream:true
